events.title: Lee Surrenders at Appomattox Court House
events.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Union General Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia.
events.significance: The surrender effectively marked the end of the American Civil War, though some Confederate forces continued fighting for several weeks. It paved the way for national reunification and Reconstruction.

events.title: Germany Invades Denmark and Norway
events.description: Nazi Germany launched Operation Weserübung, invading Denmark and Norway. Denmark capitulated within hours, while Norway resisted for about two months.
events.significance: The invasion secured Germany's access to Scandinavian resources, particularly Swedish iron ore, and to Atlantic naval bases, and expanded the war in Europe in World War II.

events.title: Ratification Era: Passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1866 over Presidential Veto
events.description: On April 9, 1866, the U.S. Congress overrode President Andrew Johnson's veto to pass the Civil Rights Act of 1866, the first major law passed over a presidential veto.
events.significance: The act declared all persons born in the United States to be citizens and laid the groundwork for the Fourteenth Amendment, shaping American civil rights law.

events.title: NASA Introduces the Mercury Seven Astronauts
events.description: NASA publicly introduced its first seven astronauts, the Mercury Seven, at a press conference in Washington, D.C.: Scott Carpenter, Gordon Cooper, John Glenn, Gus Grissom, Wally Schirra, Alan Shepard, and Deke Slayton.
events.significance: The announcement marked the beginning of the American human spaceflight program and made the astronauts national heroes during the Space Race.

events.title: First Boeing 737 Rolls Out
events.description: Boeing unveiled the first 737 airliner at its Renton, Washington factory, designed as a short-to-medium-range twin-engine jet.
events.significance: The 737 became one of the best-selling commercial aircraft in history and a mainstay of global air travel for decades.
